title: OpenCode Sandbox trusted policy
description: Trusted policy file opencode-sandbox.json. The plugin rejects unknown keys. This editor schema checks value shapes and selected cross-field constraints; filesystem ownership, canonical paths and OS sandbox rules are validated at runtime.

$schema.description: Optional schema URI for editor tooling only; the plugin never fetches it or uses it for runtime security decisions.

network.description: Whether sandboxed shell commands can access the network. 'allow' permits unrestricted shell network access, not just GitHub.

mode.description: In enforce mode, shell commands are refused if the sandbox cannot start. Permissive mode is a global sandbox opt-out.

writablePaths.description: Additional existing host paths writable by sandboxed commands. Relative paths resolve against the workspace. The host home, sensitive credential directories and protected system paths are not eligible.

readablePaths.description: Additional host paths readable inside the sandbox, including explicitly trusted credential paths. Path existence and conflicts with writable paths are checked at runtime.

passEnv.description: Host environment variable names passed to sandboxed commands. Reserved environment keys cannot be overridden. Avoid passing secrets unless explicitly necessary.

shell.description: Absolute path to the shell used inside the sandbox (Linux/macOS/WSL).

toolGuard.description: Apply policy checks to OpenCode file tools and webfetch; off disables this in-process guard but not the shell sandbox.

webfetch.description: Allow or deny the OpenCode webfetch tool. Requires toolGuard=enforce when set to deny.

items.description: Plain hostname, e.g. github.com or *.github.com; not a URL. A wildcard includes the apex and subdomains.

webfetchAllowlist.description: Restrict OpenCode webfetch requests to these hostnames. An empty list means no host restriction. Does not restrict shell network traffic.

deniedPaths.description: Workspace paths hidden from the sandbox and denied by the file-tool guard. Relative paths resolve against the workspace; OS-specific missing-path handling still applies.

items.description: Exact shell command or a 'prefix *' pattern. Shell metacharacters and chains are prohibited. These commands execute on the host with its full environment and permissions.

unsandboxedCommands.description: Commands explicitly permitted to bypass the shell sandbox. Prefer exact commands instead of broad wildcard prefixes, especially for credentialed CLI tools.
